source.title: Keeping an Eye on LLM Unlearning: The Hidden Risk and Remedy
source.authors: Jie Ren; Zhenwei Dai; Xianfeng Tang; Yue Xing; Shenglai Zeng; Hui Liu; Jingying Zeng; Qiankun Peng; Samarth Varshney; Suhang Wang; Qi He; Charu C. Aggarwal; Hui Liu

record.file_problem: None; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper relies on prior work’s account of unlearning signals and develops a new attack and defense for benign-trigger utility degradation. It does not test whether the attacks in the claim recover forgotten targeted knowledge.
record.gate_note: The paper’s own Stealthy Attack (SA) results measure utility on normal inputs containing benign trigger tokens after the forgetting corpus was modified to include those tokens. This is not recovery of the forgotten knowledge. The paper’s explanation that unlearning can memorize signals, and its descriptions of prior work, do not provide new recovery results. Rows below record the SA trigger-utility comparisons and the related unlearning and clean-utility metrics from Table 2; the SU rows record trigger utility under the paper’s new defense.
record.test_reason: The paper is mainly about a benign-trigger utility attack (SA) and a defense (SU), which fit no version. One result does bear on B: Table 4's continuous fine-tuning baseline is unrelated to the claim's attacks. It fine-tunes unlearned TOFU models on an auxiliary synthetic fake-book/author set. Forget-set ROUGE-L recall then rises from near zero to about 0.30–0.36. That is partial recovery of unlearned knowledge from a loosely related relearning set. It is an incidental baseline, not a designed recovery test.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that benign tokens can be turned into unlearning signals that degrade utility for normal users while clean utility stays intact. They conclude that SU largely restores robustness. They also note in passing that continuous fine-tuning erases the intended unlearning effect.
record.recipe_differences: The study tests a newly proposed benign-trigger data attack and Scope-aware Unlearning, not the recovery recipes named in the claim. Its experiments use GD, NPO, and IDK unlearning.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported trigger-utility degradation varies with model, unlearning method, and forgotten-data fraction; the authors note it is generally more pronounced with 10% than 5% forgetting data for NPO on LLaMA.

fits_no_version.finding: SA lowers benign-trigger utility across TOFU models and methods while clean utility stays largely unchanged.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Raising benign-token frequency in forget data makes those tokens act as unlearning triggers that degrade utility.

fits_no_version.finding: SU restores benign-trigger utility under SA, often incompletely on Mistral.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A scope term in the unlearning objective localizes the forgetting effect and reduces trigger-induced utility loss.

record.peer_reviewed: Neural Information Processing Systems (venue supplied); the text identifies the manuscript as a preprint.
record.problems: The tested attack is a benign-trigger utility-degradation attack, not an attack to recover forgotten target knowledge. Results use TOFU for the primary tables; the text reports averages over five random seeds and provides standard deviations in an appendix, but the values are not reproduced in these rows.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 clean-utility and unlearning-effectiveness values, Table 4 defense comparisons, LoRA results in Table 5, RWKU results in Table 8, and additional probability/truth-ratio results in Tables 10–13 are not included; they concern the paper’s SA/SU utility attack rather than recovery of forgotten targeted knowledge. Cited results from prior work are also excluded.

untested.parts: Only via the incidental continuous fine-tuning baseline. No prompting, quantization or internal-edit attacks, and no WMDP-style near-chance multiple-choice accuracy.
Size of the relearning set, forget fraction (5% vs 10%) and per-model baselines for the Table 4 fine-tuning are not specified. A forget-fact subset as the relearning set is not tested.
No activation ablation or internal analysis of whether knowledge is blocked or deleted. The 'unlearning signal' account is cited from prior work.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery test. The benign-trigger templates degrade retained utility; they do not recover forgotten knowledge.
SU is evaluated only against SA, not against the recovery attacks. Its resistance to relearning is not reported.

missing.what: Forget-set ROUGE-L after continuous fine-tuning on an auxiliary synthetic set. LLaMA 0.343 (GD 0.358/NPO 0.310/IDK 0.362); Mistral 0.304 (0.323/0.368/0.220). Compare SU 0.161/0.014 and the Table 2 post-unlearning values. This is a relearning-style recovery result.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T4/uses_without_test is close, but it misses the Table 4 continuous fine-tuning result. That result shows forget-set recall partially returning after benign fine-tuning; the authors frame it as a defense's cost, not an attack. The relearning set is fake books/authors from the same synthetic distribution as TOFU, so it is loosely related data. The forget fraction behind Table 4 is not stated. All existing rows are correctly unlinked to versions.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether an unlearning method reaches near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy while preserving general ability and resisting recovery attacks.
No fine-tuning recovery attack with unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples is tested.
No activation-direction ablation or internal-edit recovery test is performed.
No quantization recovery test is performed.

Benign trigger tokens in prompts cause utility degradation; the paper does not test whether rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information recover the forgotten targeted knowledge.
Scope-aware Unlearning (SU) is tested against this paper’s SA, not against the recovery attacks named in the claim.

relationships.condition: LLaMA 3.1 8B and Mistral 7B on TOFU, after GD/NPO/IDK unlearning under SA, then fine-tuned on an auxiliary synthetic fake-book/author set
relationships.reason: Text-based (Table 4; no row records it). Forget ROUGE-L rises to 0.343 (LLaMA) and 0.304 (Mistral) from near zero for GD/IDK. Pre-unlearning value was about 0.99, so recovery is partial, roughly one third.
relationships.display_finding: Forget ROUGE-L rose from near zero to 0.343 for LLaMA and 0.304 for Mistral after GD/IDK, compared with about 0.99 before unlearning.

relationships.reason: Text-based (Table 4). A simple benign fine-tuning step undoes part of the forgetting: GD 0.358 and IDK 0.362 forget ROUGE on LLaMA, versus ≤0.03 after unlearning (Table 2).
relationships.display_finding: Forget ROUGE rose from at most 0.03 after unlearning to 0.358 for GD and 0.362 for IDK on LLaMA.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
